flexible disk cartridges recorded at 7 958 ftprad on both sides using modified frequency modulation (MFM) recording. IS0 7497/l specifies the dimensional, physical, and magnetic characteristics of the cartridge so as to provide physical interchangeability between data processing systems. IS0 7497/2 specifies an alternative track format for data interchange. Together with the Isbelling scheme specified in IS0 7665, IS0 7497/l and IS0 7497/3 provide for full data interchange between data processing systems.

Scope and field of application

IS0 7665, information processing - File structure and lab&ng of flexible disk cartridges for inform&on interchange.

4.1

Track format
General requirements
Mode of recording

system in this International Standard may have been rounded off and therefore are consistent with, but not exactly equal to, each other. Either system may be used, but the two should be neither intermixed nor re-converted. The original design of this part of IS0 7487 was made using SI units.

4.1.1

The mode of recording shall be Modified Frequency Modulation (MFM) for which the conditions are a) a flux transition shall be written at the centre of each bit cell containing a ONE; b) a flux transition shalj be written at each cell boundary between consecutive bit cells containing ZERO's. Exceptions to this are defined in 4.1.12.

2

Conformance

A flexible disk cartridge shall be in conformance with IS0 7487 when it meets all requirements either of parts 1 and 2 or of parts 1 and 3 of IS0 7487.

This field shall specify in binary notation the cylinder address from 00 for the outermost cylinder to 37 for the innermost cylinder. b) Side number

(Side)

At nominal density this field shall comprise not less than 32 bytes and not more than 146 bytes, the content of which is not specified except that there shall be no (Al)*-bytes.

The 3rd byte shall specify in binary notation the sector number from 01 for the 1st sector to 16 for the last sector.

Annex A EDC implementation
(This annex does not form part of the standard.)

Figure 5 shows the feedback connections of a shift register which may be used to generate the EDC bytes. Prior to the operation, all positions of the shiftregister are set to ONE. Input data are added (exclusive OR) to the contents of position Cts of the register to form a feedback. This feedback is in its turn added (exclusive OR) to the contents of position Cd and position Ct,. On shifting, the outputs of the exclusive OR gates are entered respectively into positions Cs, Ca and Ct2. After the last data bit has been added, the register is shifted once more as specified above. The register then contains the EDC bytes. If further shifting is to take place during the writing of the EDC bytes, the control signal inhibits exclusive OR operations. To check for errors when reading, the data bits are added into the shift register in exactly the same manner as they were during writing. After the data, the EDC bytes are also entered into the shift register as if they were data. After the final shift, the register contents will be all ZERO if the record does not contain errors.

(EDC writing) Figure 5

Annex B Procedure and equipment for measuring flux transition spacing

(This annex does not form part of the standard.)

B.l

General

This annex specifies-an equipment and a procedure for measuring flux transition spacing on 130 mm (5.25 in) flexible disk cartridges using MFM recording at 7 858 ftprad on two sides.

B.2

Format

The disk to be-measured shall be written by the disk drive for data interchange use. Testing shall be done on tracks 00 and 38 on both sides. The test patterns 11011011 (DB) and 11011100 (DC) shall be written repeatedly on each test track.

B.3
8.3.1

Test equipment
Disk drive

The disk drive shall have a rotational speed of 300 rlmin, with a tolerance of f 3 r/min, averaged over one revolution. The average angular speed taken over 64 us shall not deviate by more than 0.5 % from the speed averaged over one revolution.

8.3.2 -8.3.2.1

Head
Resolution

The head shall have an absolute resolution of 55 % to 65 % at track 38 on each side, using the reference material RM 7487, applying the calibration factor of the reference material appropriate to the side, and recording with the appropriate test recording current. The resonant frequency of the head shall be at least 250 Ooo Hz. The resolution shall not be adjusted by varying the load impedance of the head. The resolution shall be measured at the output of the amplifier defined in 6.3.3.1. 8.3.2.2 Offset angle

The head shall have a gap offset angle of O" + ~6' with the disk radius on the testing drive. 8.3.2.3 Contact

Care shall be taken that the headsare in good contact with the media~during the tests. 8.3.3 8.3.3.1 Read channel

Read amplifier

The read amplifier shall have a flat response from 1 000 to 187 560 Hz within + 1 dB, and amplitude saturation shall not occur. 8.3.3.2 Peak sensing amplifier

Peak sensing shall Abecarried out by a differentiating and limiting amplifier.

8.3.4

Time interval

measuring

equipment

The time interval counter shall be able to measure 4 us to at least 10 ns resolution.
A triggering oscilloscope may be used for this purpose.

B.4
B.4.1

Procedure

for measurement
spacing measurement

Flux transition

The transition locations shall be measured by the locations of the peaks in the signal when reading. The flux transition spacing shall be measured by the pulse timing intervals after the read channel amplifier defined in 8.33. B.4.2 Flux transition

.

spacing for all tracks

Annex Data separators

C MFM recording

for decoding

(This annex does not form part of the standard.)

The MFM recording method gives nominal flux transition spacings of :

I for the patterns 1 1 or 0 0 0
3r/2 for the patterns 1 0 or 0 1 2r for the pattern 1 0 1 The data separator should~be capable of resolving a difference of 2 us. To achieve this with a low error rate, the separator cannot operate on a fixed period but should follow changes in the bit cell length. It is recognized that various techniques may be developed to achieve dynamic data separation; with present technology only an analogue data separator based on a phase-locked oscillator can provide the necessary reliability.
